intlFaqs.q: What is the process like for patients from abroad?
intlFaqs.a: Your journey begins with an expert case review, which can be initiated online. Our team evaluates your medical information and provides clear guidance on next steps before any trip is planned.
Yes. Initial consultations and case reviews can be carried out online, allowing you to receive expert guidance without traveling until it is truly necessary.

intlFaqs.q: Is support offered to help prepare for the trip?
intlFaqs.a: Yes. Our international patient team assists with:
list: Guidance on timing and duration of stay
Communication in English throughout the process
intlFaqs.foot: Our goal is to make the process as smooth and predictable as possible.

intlFaqs.a: The initial expert case review is offered without obligation. Any subsequent steps are clearly explained in advance so you can make informed decisions.

intlFaqs.q: Who will support me during the process?
list: A medical team specialized in your case
English-speaking staff available throughout your journey
intlFaqs.foot: You are never navigating the process alone.

faqs.q: What should I do after a failed IVF cycle?
faqs.a: The most important step is a thorough review of what happened. Repeating the same protocol without understanding why it failed rarely changes the outcome. A second opinion can help identify factors that were previously overlooked.
PGT-A is recommended only when it can provide meaningful information about embryo viability or help guide treatment decisions. It is not necessary in all cases.

faqs.q: When should I seek a second opinion?
faqs.a: When explanations have not been clear, when the same protocol is repeated without changes, or when results don’t align with what would be expected for your situation.

faqs.q: Is egg donation always the only option for women over 40?
faqs.a: No. Egg donation is considered only when the chances of success with one’s own eggs are very low. It is discussed transparently and respectfully, based on individual circumstances.

faqs.q: Can IVF failure be related to genetic causes?
faqs.a: Yes. In some cases, genetic factors can affect embryo development or implantation. When appropriate, genetic studies such as PGT-A may help clarify the situation and guide decisions.
No. Genetic tests are recommended only when they can add clarity or change the treatment strategy. The decision is always explained and made together with the patient.

faqs.q: Is it possible to get pregnant with my own eggs after 40?
faqs.a: Yes. In some cases, genetic factors can affect embryo development or implantation. When appropriate, genetic studies such as PGT-A may help clarify the situation and guide decisions.

faqs.q: Does a second opinion really improve the chances of success?
faqs.a: It can, when it helps correct strategy, identify hidden factors, or avoid repeating ineffective approaches.
